Walkthrough
The PR adds ADR 0013, which classifies persisted data by storage tier and defines sync rules. It updates the architecture guide, changelog, migration-lot catalog, and settings catalog to document related KVS, MPStorage, and Keychain scopes. **Changes: Storage tiers and sync documentation** |Layer / File(s)|Summary| |:---|:---| |**Storage-tier contract and platform rules**

The architecture guide documents KVS implementations and excludes secrets from that store.| |**Account and MPStorage sync rules**
`docs/adr/0013-storage-tiers.md`, `docs/LOTS.md`, `docs/CHANGELOG-LEGACY.md`|The documentation describes per-account MPStorage activation and merge behavior, opt-in Keychain account sync, and optional app lock.| |**Settings, lists, and reading-position scopes**
`docs/lots/LOT-060-settings-store.md`, `docs/LOTS.md`, `README.md`, `docs/CHANGELOG-LEGACY.md`|The documentation records synced settings and KVS scopes for selected lists and fine reading positions. It updates the migration-lot count and dates.| Priority: Low **Estimated code review effort:** 2 (Simple) | ~10 minutes **Change:** Other **Possibly related issues** - [ezzz/HFRnow#311](https://github.com/ezzz/HFRnow/issues/311) — The PR documents iCloud KVS scope and sync rules. - [ezzz/HFRnow#182](https://github.com/ezzz/HFRnow/issues/182) — The PR documents the KVS mirror for fine reading position. - [ezzz/HFRnow#92](https://github.com/ezzz/HFRnow/issues/92) — ADR 0013 documents the legacy import order, but does not implement the import. - [ezzz/HFRnow#89](https://github.com/ezzz/HFRnow/issues/89) — ADR 0013 assigns super-favourites and app-local smiley favourites to iCloud KVS. - [ezzz/HFRnow#248](https://github.com/ezzz/HFRnow/issues/248) — ADR 0013 documents legacy import order, but does not implement first-launch import. - [ezzz/HFRnow#310](https://github.com/ezzz/HFRnow/issues/310) — ADR 0013 records that the allowlist remains in iCloud KVS until a shared MPStorage namespace contract exists. - [ezzz/HFRnow#221](https://github.com/ezzz/HFRnow/issues/221) — ADR 0013 assigns the blacklist to MPStorage and defines per-account sync state. - [ezzz/HFRnow#312](https://github.com/ezzz/HFRnow/issues/312) — ADR 0013 documents opt-in iCloud Keychain account sync and app-lock rules. **Possibly related PRs** - [ezzz/HFRnow#280](https://github.com/ezzz/HFRnow/pull/280) — Both PRs update the README migration-lot audit count. - [ezzz/HFRnow#271](https://github.com/ezzz/HFRnow/pull/271) — This PR adds storage behavior entries to the legacy changelog introduced by PR `#271`. - [ezzz/HFRnow#292](https://github.com/ezzz/HFRnow/pull/292) — This PR documents storage scopes for settings implemented through `SettingKey` and `SettingsStore`.
Merge Risk: Moderate · up to a0ce1
This PR only changes documentation, but the credential-sync opt-out design in ADR 0013 has gaps that could let account sync stay on or turn back on after a user disables it. Fix the tombstone ordering rule and the bootstrap rule in the ADR before implementation of the Keychain sync lot begins.
Security architecture risk: Low · up to a0ce1
The PR does not change running storage code, and most ownership and migration rules are explicit. However, the credential-sync contract has inconsistent opt-out transitions that should be resolved before implementation. **Retained concerns** - **Medium · security · observed:** The accepted credential-sync contract does not consistently preserve opt-out tombstone dominance. Bootstrap imports any synchronizable item and enables sync, without distinguishing a credential envelope from a tombstone. Race repair also preserves deletedAt while expecting it to exceed the racing device's lastPushed; a stale write completed after deletion can make lastPushed later than deletedAt, so the stated switch-off condition no longer follows. The separate rule that only explicit switch-on may overwrite a tombstone is protective, but leaves these transitions contradictory rather than fully specified. Implementations could disagree about consent and opt-out enforcement across credential-bearing devices.
Security review details
**Security Blast Radius** - _observed_ — Credential replication operates on the whole account envelope across the user's iCloud Keychain devices. Imported cookies retain session authority without another login. Switching synchronization off preserves device-only credentials, so it is not a remote logout or session-revocation mechanism. **Security Findings and Attack Paths** - _inferred_ — The identified risk concerns already participating credential-sync devices and their recovery transitions, not an established unauthenticated entrypoint. An implementation following the ambiguous bootstrap or timestamp rules could fail to converge on the user's opt-out decision; runtime credential disclosure has not been demonstrated. **Trust Boundaries and Controls** - _observed_ — The design distinguishes HFR-account ownership from Apple-ID ownership. KVS account changes isolate old pending data; credential replication requires opt-in and uses encrypted iCloud Keychain transport. Ordinary credential changes are expressly forbidden from recreating an absent synchronizable item or overriding an opt-out tombstone. **Resilience and Maintainability Implications** - _observed_ — The credential contract explicitly anticipates delayed delivery, absent items and non-conditional Keychain writes. Read-compare-write and periodic tombstone repair are meaningful safeguards, but their bootstrap and ordering conditions need reconciliation to establish the promised opt-out convergence. **Hardening Proposals** - _proposed_ — Define tombstone-aware bootstrap and one consistent opt-out ordering rule independent of a racing push timestamp. Validate the contract against delayed delivery, stale writes after deletion, repeated repair and a genuinely later explicit re-enable action before implementing credential replication.

**Operator decisions on the Opus review (2026-10-29), recorded by the steward.** These replace the open questions of findings 2–4 of [the review at a0ce168](https://github.com/ezzz/HFRnow/pull/313#pullrequestreview-5685340190).

- **F2 (theme): parity.** Keep every theme colour already decided, following LOT-121 "Theme parity". They are only accents, so all of them ship at once. The single `accent` key goes away, and FEAT-010's single accent stays out of scope.
- **F3 (super-favourites and smiley favourites): per HFR account.**
  - The ADR states this in §5 and the budget.
  - The legacy keys `SuperFavoritesIds` and `smiley_favorites_cache2` are global. They are imported into the account that is active at the first import (steward's default; the operator may override).
  - Add a CHANGELOG-LEGACY row for the global → per-account change.
- **F4 (Keychain opt-out): full activation timestamp (`enabledAt`), no generation counter.** The rules, all failing closed:
  - Compare the tombstone's `deletedAt` with the device's **local `enabledAt`**, never with `lastPushed`.
  - A device whose `enabledAt` is not strictly later than `deletedAt` switches off. A tie also switches off.
  - Bootstrap imports only a full synchronizable envelope whose `enabledAt` is later than every known `deletedAt`. A tombstone keeps the switch off, records `honouredDeletedAt`, and creates no device-only item.
  - Only an explicit switch-on overwrites a tombstone.
  - Accepted residual risk: if a device's clock runs ahead, an earlier switch-on can outrank a later opt-out. The fail-closed rules and the user's own devices running on network time keep that window small.
- **F1, F5, F6: mechanical**, still to apply:
  - F1: bring #311, #312 and the #220 comment in line with the ADR.
  - F5: mark `embedded_videos` as dropped.
  - F6: freeze the account key form, or require a migration when LOT-072 lands.

Whoever applies them should first check which findings head `3248550` already closes. A re-review then follows. Routing is posted separately.

**Findings F1–F6**

- **F1 — fixed** (issue bodies, with the operator's authorisation; each body backed up before the edit, re-read after): #311 (`AccountChange` now quarantines per ADR §3, in scope and acceptance criteria; the account key and the import target of the legacy global lists are stated; theme parity and `embedded_videos` in the `Setting.scope` criterion; a test pins the account key), #312 (switch-off writes a tombstone and never deletes the item, in the first scope bullet and the first acceptance criterion; bootstrap only above every known `deletedAt`; tie switches off; `honouredDeletedAt` on a tombstone at bootstrap; clock-skew residual risk), and the #220 comment on `mpstorage_active` (now the per-account record of ADR §7).
- **F2 — fixed**: `docs/adr/0013-storage-tiers.md:100` (§8 row: the 7 theme keys kept and synced, LOT-121 "Theme parity", FEAT-010's single accent out of scope), `:204` (matrix row), `:232` (budget: no `accent` key). The `accent` key is gone from the ADR.
- **F3 — fixed**: `0013:168` (smiley favourites per HFR account), `:63` (§5: legacy `SuperFavoritesIds` and `smiley_favorites_cache2` are global, cited at `HFRswift/Swift/Favorites.swift:133-155`, `Classes/FavoritesTableViewController.m:81-82, 1657`, `Classes/SmileyCache.m:18, 353-354` on `origin/master` @ `21173e7`; imported into the account active at the first import, steward default the operator may override); `docs/CHANGELOG-LEGACY.md:38` (row 30).
- **F4 — partly closed by 3248550** (`deletedAt` vs the local `enabledAt`, no `lastPushed`; bootstrap only from a full envelope; only an explicit switch-on overwrites a tombstone) — **remainder fixed** in `0013:74` (bootstrap only from a full envelope whose `enabledAt` is later than every known `deletedAt`; a tombstone records `honouredDeletedAt` and creates no device-only item), `:76-77` (a tie switches off, `deletedAt >= enabledAt`), `:78` (the tombstone's writer counts as having honoured it; the repair is eventual, not atomic), `:79` (clock-skew residual risk, generation counter rejected). `docs/LOTS.md:235` (LOT-173 row) says ties fail closed.
- **F5 — fixed**: `0013:209` (`embedded_videos` dropped: removed from `master` by `d645f52`, no reader nor writer at `21173e7`, checked with `git grep`), `:102` (§8 dropped list); `docs/lots/LOT-060-settings-store.md:54` (the catalogue key gets `scope: .device` until the "not ported" list removes it).
- **F6 — fixed** by freezing the key form: `0013:89`. Frozen rather than migrated because a KVS key migration cannot be ordered across the devices of one Apple ID (last-writer-wins per key, no cross-device ordering): a device on an older build would keep writing the old keys and the two sets would diverge silently. LOT-172 keeps its own `accountKey` function pinned by a table-driven test; LOT-072 (#96) leaves it alone.

comments.body:
**Operator decision (2026-10-29), on finding 1 of the review at fffadde:** the residual risk is **accepted**.

The case: a fresh device bootstraps from a raced stale envelope, and its provisional window ends before the race repair arrives. That device then switches off, but keeps the imported credentials. They stay on the user's own Apple-ID devices only.

This decision is recorded in ADR §6 next to the clock-skew risk, and in #312. The two Low findings go to the LOT-173 spec as acceptance criteria in #312:
- the tie on `updatedAt` after a merge;
- the per-account consent rule, so that an account deleted on another device is not brought back by a merge;
- "a repair after the provisional window deletes nothing".

+# 0013 — Where persisted data lives: MPStorage, iCloud key-value store, or the device
+
+**Status:** Accepted — 2026-10-28 (operator decisions of 2026-10-28; drafted by session `mac/storage-adr-fable`)
+
+## Context
+
+The legacy app keeps its data in four places (audit [E §2–3](../audit/E-storage-vendors.md)): the Keychain (accounts), `UserDefaults` (≈ 60 keys: preferences, counters, UI state, the composer draft), files in `Documents/` (blacklist, allowlist, smiley favourites, rehost history) and **MPStorage**, a private-message thread used as a JSON document (`Classes/MPStorage.m`, [HFR-PROTOCOL §3.3](../HFR-PROTOCOL.md#33-mpstorage-bookmarks-synced-blacklist-mp-flags)). MPStorage is the only store that follows the **HFR account** across devices and clients: the document is also written by web userscripts (DTCloud and others, 13+ namespaces in one real document) and read by the Android client redface2 ([research](../research/redface2-comparison.md) E23, C8). It is also the most fragile: one thread, whole-document read-modify-write, a 64 KiB cap shared by every writer, no locking (LOT-062 adds a three-way merge).
+
+Nothing follows the **Apple ID** today: no App Group, no iCloud (audit E §2). A user with an iPhone and an iPad configures the app twice and loses the allowlist, super-favourites and smiley favourites on a new device (audit E §4.2).
+
+The operator asked (2026-10-28) for a matrix deciding what belongs in MPStorage and what can live on the phone and be backed up or synced through iCloud, by transferability from one platform to another, with simplifications. The lots that persist data (LOT-060 settings, 061 lists, 063 drafts, 064 small stores, 065 accounts, 066 caches, 067 import, 090 reading positions, 091 notification ledger, 119 settings screen, 130 MPStorage sync) need one rule instead of one decision each.
+
+Constraints: AGENTS.md rule 3 (no new dependency), rule 4 (no secrets outside the Keychain), the module boundaries of [ADR 0001](0001-modular-swift-packages.md) and [ADR 0008](0008-hfrclient-orchestration-module.md) (HFRStorage stays Foundation-only and builds on Linux), the Keychain accessibility decided for accounts (Q-9: this device only), the `NSUbiquitousKeyValueStore` limits (1 MB and 1024 keys per app, last-writer-wins per key).
+
+## Decision
+
+### 1. Four tiers, chosen by transferability first
+
+| Tier | Follows | Used for |
+|---|---|---|
+| **MPStorage** | the HFR account, every client | data another HFR client already reads or writes under the v0.1 schema: `blacklist`, `bookmarks`, `mpFlags`; every foreign namespace is preserved verbatim and never modelled |
+| **iCloud key-value store** (`NSUbiquitousKeyValueStore`) | the Apple ID, SwiftHFR on iPhone/iPad/Mac | small, low-churn **content preferences**, the three Apple-only lists (allowlist, super-favourites, app-local smiley favourites) and the **fine reading position** (page, last message seen, scroll offset) |
+| **Device, backed up** (UserDefaults, `Application Support/`, `Documents/`) | one device, restored by a device backup | device presentation and capability preferences, transient UI state, drafts, counters, histories, local copies and merge bases of the two tiers above |
+| **Device, not backed up** (`Library/Caches/`, Keychain `ThisDeviceOnly`) | one device | caches, offline pages, **accounts and cookies** (plus an opt-in synchronizable copy, §6) |
+
+The rules, in order:
+
+1. **Transferability.** If another platform reads or writes the item today under a known schema, it goes to MPStorage, wire-compatible, and nowhere else as a master. If no other platform has the feature, it never enters MPStorage on our own initiative: a new namespace in a document shared by 13 writers needs a contract with the other clients first ([#310](https://github.com/ezzz/HFRnow/issues/310) for the allowlist and super-favourites, with the Android app's maintainers; the userscripts' `superFavs` and `lastRead` namespaces are revisited once a real document is captured, [#272](https://github.com/ezzz/HFRnow/issues/272)).
+2. **Privacy.** Secrets (cookies, `hash_check`) stay in the Keychain and never enter MPStorage or iCloud KVS. Personal data that identifies other members (blacklist, allowlist) may sync because both stores are private to the user; unsent drafts and upload histories do not leave the device.
+3. **Size and churn.** iCloud KVS gets only values that stay far under the quota (budget in the appendix: < 200 KiB, < 60 keys for five accounts) and that change at human speed. The fine reading position is the one exception, admitted because the operator wants it on every Apple device: it is debounced and bounded (LOT-172). Drafts, counters and histories are device-only. Anything large or rebuildable (caches, offline pages) is device-only and excluded from backup.
+4. **Device semantics.** A preference whose right value depends on the device (icon, haptics, rotation, density, text size, cellular policy, badges) stays on the device even if small.
+
+The item-by-item application is the matrix in the appendix: the registry of persisted items. A lot that persists something new picks a tier by these rules and adds its row. The split for settings becomes an attribute of `Setting<Value>` (LOT-060): `scope: .synced | .device`.
+
+### 2. One master per item
+
+An item has exactly one authoritative store and at most one local copy:

+# 0013 — Where persisted data lives: MPStorage, iCloud key-value store, or the device
+
+**Status:** Accepted — 2026-10-28 (operator decisions of 2026-10-28; drafted by session `mac/storage-adr-fable`)

+## Context
+
+The legacy app keeps its data in four places (audit [E §2–3](../audit/E-storage-vendors.md)): the Keychain (accounts), `UserDefaults` (≈ 60 keys: preferences, counters, UI state, the composer draft), files in `Documents/` (blacklist, allowlist, smiley favourites, rehost history) and **MPStorage**, a private-message thread used as a JSON document (`Classes/MPStorage.m`, [HFR-PROTOCOL §3.3](../HFR-PROTOCOL.md#33-mpstorage-bookmarks-synced-blacklist-mp-flags)). +
+Nothing follows the **Apple ID** today: no App Group, no iCloud (audit E §2). A user with an iPhone and an iPad configures the app twice and loses the allowlist, super-favourites and smiley favourites on a new device (audit E §4.2).
+

+| **Device, backed up** (UserDefaults, `Application Support/`, `Documents/`) | one device, restored by a device backup | device presentation and capability preferences, transient UI state, drafts, counters, histories, local copies and merge bases of the two tiers above |
+| **Device, not backed up** (`Library/Caches/`, Keychain `ThisDeviceOnly`) | one device | caches, offline pages, **accounts and cookies** (plus an opt-in synchronizable copy, §6) |

+
+1. **Transferability.** If another platform reads or writes the item today under a known schema, it goes to MPStorage, wire-compatible, and nowhere else as a master. +

+

+# 0013 — Where persisted data lives: MPStorage, iCloud key-value store, or the device
+
+**Status:** Accepted — 2026-10-28 (operator decisions of 2026-10-28; drafted by session `mac/storage-adr-fable`)
+
+## Context
+
+The legacy app keeps its data in four places (audit [E §2–3](../audit/E-storage-vendors.md)): the Keychain (accounts), `UserDefaults` (≈ 60 keys: preferences, counters, UI state, the composer draft), files in `Documents/` (blacklist, allowlist, smiley favourites, rehost history) and **MPStorage**, a private-message thread used as a JSON document (`Classes/MPStorage.m`, [HFR-PROTOCOL §3.3](../HFR-PROTOCOL.md#33-mpstorage-bookmarks-synced-blacklist-mp-flags)). MPStorage is the only store that follows the **HFR account** across devices and clients: the document is also written by web userscripts (DTCloud and others, 13+ namespaces in one real document) and read by the Android client redface2 ([research](../research/redface2-comparison.md) E23, C8). It is also the most fragile: one thread, whole-document read-modify-write, a 64 KiB cap shared by every writer, no locking (LOT-062 adds a three-way merge).
+
+Nothing follows the **Apple ID** today: no App Group, no iCloud (audit E §2). A user with an iPhone and an iPad configures the app twice and loses the allowlist, super-favourites and smiley favourites on a new device (audit E §4.2).
+
+The operator asked (2026-10-28) for a matrix deciding what belongs in MPStorage and what can live on the phone and be backed up or synced through iCloud, by transferability from one platform to another, with simplifications. The lots that persist data (LOT-060 settings, 061 lists, 063 drafts, 064 small stores, 065 accounts, 066 caches, 067 import, 090 reading positions, 091 notification ledger, 119 settings screen, 130 MPStorage sync) need one rule instead of one decision each.
+
+Constraints: AGENTS.md rule 3 (no new dependency), rule 4 (no secrets outside the Keychain), the module boundaries of [ADR 0001](0001-modular-swift-packages.md) and [ADR 0008](0008-hfrclient-orchestration-module.md) (HFRStorage stays Foundation-only and builds on Linux), the Keychain accessibility decided for accounts (Q-9: this device only), the `NSUbiquitousKeyValueStore` limits (1 MB and 1024 keys per app, last-writer-wins per key).
+
+## Decision
+
+### 1. Four tiers, chosen by transferability first
+
+| Tier | Follows | Used for |
+|---|---|---|
+| **MPStorage** | the HFR account, every client | data another HFR client already reads or writes under the v0.1 schema: `blacklist`, `bookmarks`, `mpFlags`; every foreign namespace is preserved verbatim and never modelled |
+| **iCloud key-value store** (`NSUbiquitousKeyValueStore`) | the Apple ID, SwiftHFR on iPhone/iPad/Mac | small, low-churn **content preferences**, the three Apple-only lists (allowlist, super-favourites, app-local smiley favourites) and the **fine reading position** (page, last message seen, scroll offset) |
+| **Device, backed up** (UserDefaults, `Application Support/`, `Documents/`) | one device, restored by a device backup | device presentation and capability preferences, transient UI state, drafts, counters, histories, local copies and merge bases of the two tiers above |
+| **Device, not backed up** (`Library/Caches/`, Keychain `ThisDeviceOnly`) | one device | caches, offline pages, **accounts and cookies** (plus an opt-in synchronizable copy, §6) |
+
+The rules, in order:
+
+1. **Transferability.** If another platform reads or writes the item today under a known schema, it goes to MPStorage, wire-compatible, and nowhere else as a master. If no other platform has the feature, it never enters MPStorage on our own initiative: a new namespace in a document shared by 13 writers needs a contract with the other clients first ([#310](https://github.com/ezzz/HFRnow/issues/310) for the allowlist and super-favourites, with the Android app's maintainers; the userscripts' `superFavs` and `lastRead` namespaces are revisited once a real document is captured, [#272](https://github.com/ezzz/HFRnow/issues/272)).
+2. **Privacy.** Secrets (cookies, `hash_check`) stay in the Keychain and never enter MPStorage or iCloud KVS. Personal data that identifies other members (blacklist, allowlist) may sync because both stores are private to the user; unsent drafts and upload histories do not leave the device.
+3. **Size and churn.** iCloud KVS gets only values that stay far under the quota (budget in the appendix: < 200 KiB, < 60 keys for five accounts) and that change at human speed. The fine reading position is the one exception, admitted because the operator wants it on every Apple device: it is debounced and bounded (LOT-172). Drafts, counters and histories are device-only. Anything large or rebuildable (caches, offline pages) is device-only and excluded from backup.
+4. **Device semantics.** A preference whose right value depends on the device (icon, haptics, rotation, density, text size, cellular policy, badges) stays on the device even if small.
+
+The item-by-item application is the matrix in the appendix: the registry of persisted items. A lot that persists something new picks a tier by these rules and adds its row. The split for settings becomes an attribute of `Setting<Value>` (LOT-060): `scope: .synced | .device`.
+
+### 2. One master per item
+
+An item has exactly one authoritative store and at most one local copy:
+
+- MPStorage items: the forum document is the master; the device keeps the last document read (`base` for LOT-062's merge) and the pending edits. Reads come from the local copy; writes are local-first and synced when a session is available (legacy's sync-first add, which aborted the local change on a network error, is dropped: audit E §7 item 6). On a successful remote read the local list is **merged**, not replaced (legacy `MPStorage.m:202-215` replaced it; audit Q-4).
+- iCloud KVS items: KVS is the master; `UserDefaults` is the mirror that `@AppStorage` and the synchronous `SettingsStore` read. A write goes to both; an external-change notification updates the mirror. The engine never reads KVS on the hot path.
+- A device-only item has no copy.
+
+### 3. Conflict policy
+
+| Store | Policy | Why |
+|---|---|---|
+| MPStorage | per-item three-way merge of LOT-062 (`base`, `ours`, `theirs`), ours wins when both changed, tombstones off until other writers are known to keep them | already decided (LOT-062, Q-6) |
+| iCloud KVS, scalar preferences | **last writer wins per key**, as the store does; on the initial sync (`NSUbiquitousKeyValueStoreInitialSyncChange`) the cloud value wins over the local one | the only conflict is the same setting changed on two devices while offline; the later tap is the user's intent |
+| iCloud KVS, lists (allowlist, super-favourites, smiley favourites) | **last writer wins on the whole list**, each list one key holding `{version, items:[{id, addedAt}]}`; a union merge with tombstones is the documented upgrade if users report lost adds | simplification: these lists change a few times a month; a merge layer would duplicate LOT-062 for three tiny lists |
+| iCloud KVS, reading positions | last writer wins per topic key; the newest `updatedAt` is kept when both devices wrote | a position is a point in time |
+| iCloud account change (`NSUbiquitousKeyValueStoreAccountChange`, sign-out) | keep the local mirror, do not clear anything, resume with the next account's values on the next initial sync; a schema version key lets an older build ignore values it cannot read | never lose data because the Apple ID changed |
+
+### 4. Offline behaviour
+
+- MPStorage: read from the local copy; edits are queued in the local document and merged on the next successful sync; the UI shows the last sync from `mpstorage_last_rw` (persisted for real, LOT-060). A failed sync never undoes a local edit.
+- iCloud KVS: writes land in the local mirror and in the store's on-device queue; the system uploads later. The app calls `synchronize()` at launch and on foreground, and treats a missing iCloud account as "device-only" without a warning.
+- Device tiers: unaffected.
+
+### 5. Migration from the legacy app (LOT-067 and LOT-158; same bundle id, Q-1)
+
+SwiftHFR ships as an in-place update of `hfrplus.red.super` under the ezzz team, so the legacy container is readable and the legacy data is **kept** (operator 2026-10-28):
+
+1. Import everything into the **device** tiers first, with the LOT-067 plan: UserDefaults keys under their legacy names, `blackListDico.plist` / `whiteList.plist` into the LOT-061 document, `smiley_favorites_cache2` into LOT-064, `composerDraftText` into `DraftContext.legacyGlobal`, Keychain accounts into LOT-065 (device-only item).
+2. Then enable the KVS mirror: for each synced key, if the cloud has no value, push the imported one; if it has one (another device migrated first), the cloud wins (initial-sync rule). Lists follow the same rule, whole list.
+3. MPStorage needs no migration: same thread, same schema `0.1`; the document is re-read on first sync and becomes the merge base.
+4. The legacy keys dropped by LOT-060 are read once where a migration exists (`size_text_topics`), otherwise ignored; nothing is deleted from the legacy container (LOT-067 rule).
+
+### 6. Accounts: device-only by default, opt-in iCloud Keychain sync, optional app lock (Q12)
+
+Accounts stay in a device-only Keychain item (LOT-065, Q-9). Two options, both off by default, are added by LOT-173 ([#312](https://github.com/ezzz/HFRnow/issues/312)):
+
+- **"Synchroniser mes comptes via le trousseau iCloud"**: when on, the credential envelope is also written to a second, **synchronizable** Keychain item (`kSecAttrSynchronizable`, `AfterFirstUnlock`), which iCloud Keychain carries to the user's other devices end to end encrypted; the device-only item stays the local master; switching off deletes the synchronizable copy. The setting explains what travels and how to stop.
+- **App lock** (Face ID / Touch ID / device code, `LocalAuthentication`) with a grace delay, covering every scene.
+
+Nothing else about secrets changes: no password is stored, no cookie leaves the Keychain.
+
+### 7. MPStorage sync: on when the account already has a storage thread, else asked at the first write (Q14)
+
+Blacklist and bookmarks stay in MPStorage. `mpstorage_active` (synced through KVS, app-wide as in legacy) is no longer simply "off by default":
+
+- At login or first sync, LOT-130 looks for the account's storage thread (the LOT-038 scan, read-only). **Found → sync is on** for that account: the user already chose it in another client, and reading the document costs nothing.
+- **Not found → the app asks** at the first bookmark or blacklist write, because creating the thread is a write to the forum (a private message to `MultiMP`); until the user answers, the list stays device-only. Declining is remembered per account; the setting can be turned on later in Settings.

+# 0013 — Where persisted data lives: MPStorage, iCloud key-value store, or the device
+
+**Status:** Accepted — 2026-10-28 (operator decisions of 2026-10-28; drafted by session `mac/storage-adr-fable`)
+
+## Context
+
+The legacy app keeps its data in four places (audit [E §2–3](../audit/E-storage-vendors.md)): the Keychain (accounts), `UserDefaults` (≈ 60 keys: preferences, counters, UI state, the composer draft), files in `Documents/` (blacklist, allowlist, smiley favourites, rehost history) and **MPStorage**, a private-message thread used as a JSON document (`Classes/MPStorage.m`, [HFR-PROTOCOL §3.3](../HFR-PROTOCOL.md#33-mpstorage-bookmarks-synced-blacklist-mp-flags)). MPStorage is the only store that follows the **HFR account** across devices and clients: the document is also written by web userscripts (DTCloud and others, 13+ namespaces in one real document) and read by the Android client redface2 ([research](../research/redface2-comparison.md) E23, C8). It is also the most fragile: one thread, whole-document read-modify-write, a 64 KiB cap shared by every writer, no locking (LOT-062 adds a three-way merge).
+
+Nothing follows the **Apple ID** today: no App Group, no iCloud (audit E §2). A user with an iPhone and an iPad configures the app twice and loses the allowlist, super-favourites and smiley favourites on a new device (audit E §4.2).
+
+The operator asked (2026-10-28) for a matrix deciding what belongs in MPStorage and what can live on the phone and be backed up or synced through iCloud, by transferability from one platform to another, with simplifications. The lots that persist data (LOT-060 settings, 061 lists, 063 drafts, 064 small stores, 065 accounts, 066 caches, 067 import, 090 reading positions, 091 notification ledger, 119 settings screen, 130 MPStorage sync) need one rule instead of one decision each.
+
+Constraints: AGENTS.md rule 3 (no new dependency), rule 4 (no secrets outside the Keychain), the module boundaries of [ADR 0001](0001-modular-swift-packages.md) and [ADR 0008](0008-hfrclient-orchestration-module.md) (HFRStorage stays Foundation-only and builds on Linux), the Keychain accessibility decided for accounts (Q-9: this device only), the `NSUbiquitousKeyValueStore` limits (1 MB and 1024 keys per app, last-writer-wins per key).
+
+## Decision
+
+### 1. Four tiers, chosen by transferability first
+
+| Tier | Follows | Used for |
+|---|---|---|
+| **MPStorage** | the HFR account, every client | data another HFR client already reads or writes under the v0.1 schema: `blacklist`, `bookmarks`, `mpFlags`; every foreign namespace is preserved verbatim and never modelled |
+| **iCloud key-value store** (`NSUbiquitousKeyValueStore`) | the Apple ID, SwiftHFR on iPhone/iPad/Mac | small, low-churn **content preferences**, the three Apple-only lists (allowlist, super-favourites, app-local smiley favourites) and the **fine reading position** (page, last message seen, scroll offset) |
+| **Device, backed up** (UserDefaults, `Application Support/`, `Documents/`) | one device, restored by a device backup | device presentation and capability preferences, transient UI state, drafts, counters, histories, local copies and merge bases of the two tiers above |
+| **Device, not backed up** (`Library/Caches/`, Keychain `ThisDeviceOnly`) | one device | caches, offline pages, **accounts and cookies** (plus an opt-in synchronizable copy, §6) |
+
+The rules, in order:
+
+1. **Transferability.** If another platform reads or writes the item today under a known schema, it goes to MPStorage, wire-compatible, and nowhere else as a master. If no other platform has the feature, it never enters MPStorage on our own initiative: a new namespace in a document shared by 13 writers needs a contract with the other clients first ([#310](https://github.com/ezzz/HFRnow/issues/310) for the allowlist and super-favourites, with the Android app's maintainers; the userscripts' `superFavs` and `lastRead` namespaces are revisited once a real document is captured, [#272](https://github.com/ezzz/HFRnow/issues/272)).
+2. **Privacy.** Secrets (cookies, `hash_check`) stay in the Keychain and never enter MPStorage or iCloud KVS. Personal data that identifies other members (blacklist, allowlist) may sync because both stores are private to the user; unsent drafts and upload histories do not leave the device.
+3. **Size and churn.** iCloud KVS gets only values that stay far under the quota (budget in the appendix: < 200 KiB, < 60 keys for five accounts) and that change at human speed. The fine reading position is the one exception, admitted because the operator wants it on every Apple device: it is debounced and bounded (LOT-172). Drafts, counters and histories are device-only. Anything large or rebuildable (caches, offline pages) is device-only and excluded from backup.
+4. **Device semantics.** A preference whose right value depends on the device (icon, haptics, rotation, density, text size, cellular policy, badges) stays on the device even if small.
+
+The item-by-item application is the matrix in the appendix: the registry of persisted items. A lot that persists something new picks a tier by these rules and adds its row. The split for settings becomes an attribute of `Setting<Value>` (LOT-060): `scope: .synced | .device`.
+
+### 2. One master per item
+
+An item has exactly one authoritative store and at most one local copy:
+
+- MPStorage items: the forum document is the master; the device keeps the last document read (`base` for LOT-062's merge) and the pending edits. Reads come from the local copy; writes are local-first and synced when a session is available (legacy's sync-first add, which aborted the local change on a network error, is dropped: audit E §7 item 6). On a successful remote read the local list is **merged**, not replaced (legacy `MPStorage.m:202-215` replaced it; audit Q-4).
+- iCloud KVS items: KVS is the master; `UserDefaults` is the mirror that `@AppStorage` and the synchronous `SettingsStore` read. A write goes to both; an external-change notification updates the mirror. The engine never reads KVS on the hot path.
+- A device-only item has no copy.
+
+### 3. Conflict policy
+
+| Store | Policy | Why |
+|---|---|---|
+| MPStorage | per-item three-way merge of LOT-062 (`base`, `ours`, `theirs`), ours wins when both changed, tombstones off until other writers are known to keep them | already decided (LOT-062, Q-6) |
+| iCloud KVS, scalar preferences | **last writer wins per key**, as the store does; on the initial sync (`NSUbiquitousKeyValueStoreInitialSyncChange`) the cloud value wins over the local one | the only conflict is the same setting changed on two devices while offline; the later tap is the user's intent |
+| iCloud KVS, lists (allowlist, super-favourites, smiley favourites) | **last writer wins on the whole list**, each list one key holding `{version, items:[{id, addedAt}]}`; a union merge with tombstones is the documented upgrade if users report lost adds | simplification: these lists change a few times a month; a merge layer would duplicate LOT-062 for three tiny lists |
+| iCloud KVS, reading positions | last writer wins per topic key; the newest `updatedAt` is kept when both devices wrote | a position is a point in time |
+| iCloud account change (`NSUbiquitousKeyValueStoreAccountChange`, sign-out) | keep the local mirror, do not clear anything, resume with the next account's values on the next initial sync; a schema version key lets an older build ignore values it cannot read | never lose data because the Apple ID changed |

The setting explains what travels and how to stop. Rules of the copy (one item, one envelope, `updatedAt` in the envelope):
+  - *Master.* The device-only item stays the master on each device; every change to it (login, re-login, deletion, main account) is pushed to the synchronizable item while the switch is on.
+  - *Bootstrap.* A device with no device-only item that finds the synchronizable item imports it into a new device-only item and turns the switch on; the imported accounts are not logged in again (the cookies are the session).
+  - *Divergence.* On launch and on foreground, when both items exist and differ, the **newer `updatedAt` wins the whole envelope** (last writer wins, like the KVS lists): a credential refreshed on another device replaces the local copy, a device that was offline longer loses its stale copy. `AccountBook.init(accounts:)` repairs duplicates and the main flag after a replacement; accounts are never silently merged into more than the user had on the winning side.
+  - *Switching off.* Deletes the synchronizable item, which iCloud Keychain removes from every device; a device that finds its switch on and the item gone turns its switch off and keeps its device-only item. Switching off never deletes a device-only item anywhere.

@@ -0,0 +1,228 @@
+# 0013 — Where persisted data lives: MPStorage, iCloud key-value store, or the device
+
+**Status:** Accepted — 2026-10-28 (operator decisions of 2026-10-28; drafted by session `mac/storage-adr-fable`)
+
+## Context
+
+The legacy app keeps its data in four places (audit [E §2–3](../audit/E-storage-vendors.md)): the Keychain (accounts), `UserDefaults` (≈ 60 keys: preferences, counters, UI state, the composer draft), files in `Documents/` (blacklist, allowlist, smiley favourites, rehost history) and **MPStorage**, a private-message thread used as a JSON document (`Classes/MPStorage.m`, [HFR-PROTOCOL §3.3](../HFR-PROTOCOL.md#33-mpstorage-bookmarks-synced-blacklist-mp-flags)). MPStorage is the only store that follows the **HFR account** across devices and clients: the document is also written by web userscripts (DTCloud and others, 13+ namespaces in one real document) and read by the Android client redface2 ([research](../research/redface2-comparison.md) E23, C8). It is also the most fragile: one thread, whole-document read-modify-write, a 64 KiB cap shared by every writer, no locking (LOT-062 adds a three-way merge).
+
+Nothing follows the **Apple ID** today: no App Group, no iCloud (audit E §2). A user with an iPhone and an iPad configures the app twice and loses the allowlist, super-favourites and smiley favourites on a new device (audit E §4.2).
+
+The operator asked (2026-10-28) for a matrix deciding what belongs in MPStorage and what can live on the phone and be backed up or synced through iCloud, by transferability from one platform to another, with simplifications. The lots that persist data (LOT-060 settings, 061 lists, 063 drafts, 064 small stores, 065 accounts, 066 caches, 067 import, 090 reading positions, 091 notification ledger, 119 settings screen, 130 MPStorage sync) need one rule instead of one decision each.
+
+Constraints: AGENTS.md rule 3 (no new dependency), rule 4 (no secrets outside the Keychain), the module boundaries of [ADR 0001](0001-modular-swift-packages.md) and [ADR 0008](0008-hfrclient-orchestration-module.md) (HFRStorage stays Foundation-only and builds on Linux), the Keychain accessibility decided for accounts (Q-9: this device only), the `NSUbiquitousKeyValueStore` limits (1 MB and 1024 keys per app, last-writer-wins per key).
+
+## Decision
+
+### 1. Four tiers, chosen by transferability first
+
+| Tier | Follows | Used for |
+|---|---|---|
+| **MPStorage** | the HFR account, every client | data another HFR client already reads or writes under the v0.1 schema: `blacklist`, `bookmarks`, `mpFlags`; every foreign namespace is preserved verbatim and never modelled |
+| **iCloud key-value store** (`NSUbiquitousKeyValueStore`) | the Apple ID, SwiftHFR on iPhone/iPad/Mac | small, low-churn **content preferences**, the three Apple-only lists (allowlist, super-favourites, app-local smiley favourites) and the **fine reading position** (page, last message seen, scroll offset) |
+| **Device, backed up** (UserDefaults, `Application Support/`, `Documents/`) | one device, restored by a device backup | device presentation and capability preferences, transient UI state, drafts, counters, histories, local copies and merge bases of the two tiers above |
+| **Device, not backed up** (`Library/Caches/`, Keychain `ThisDeviceOnly`) | one device | caches, offline pages, **accounts and cookies** (plus an opt-in synchronizable copy, §6) |
+
+The rules, in order:
+
+1. **Transferability.** If another platform reads or writes the item today under a known schema, it goes to MPStorage, wire-compatible, and nowhere else as a master. If no other platform has the feature, it never enters MPStorage on our own initiative: a new namespace in a document shared by 13 writers needs a contract with the other clients first ([#310](https://github.com/ezzz/HFRnow/issues/310) for the allowlist and super-favourites, with the Android app's maintainers; the userscripts' `superFavs` and `lastRead` namespaces are revisited once a real document is captured, [#272](https://github.com/ezzz/HFRnow/issues/272)).
+2. **Privacy.** Secrets (cookies, `hash_check`) stay in the Keychain and never enter MPStorage or iCloud KVS. Personal data that identifies other members (blacklist, allowlist) may sync because both stores are private to the user; unsent drafts and upload histories do not leave the device.
+3. **Size and churn.** iCloud KVS gets only values that stay far under the quota (budget in the appendix: < 200 KiB, < 60 keys for five accounts) and that change at human speed. The fine reading position is the one exception, admitted because the operator wants it on every Apple device: it is debounced and bounded (LOT-172). Drafts, counters and histories are device-only. Anything large or rebuildable (caches, offline pages) is device-only and excluded from backup.
+4. **Device semantics.** A preference whose right value depends on the device (icon, haptics, rotation, density, text size, cellular policy, badges) stays on the device even if small.
+
+The item-by-item application is the matrix in the appendix: the registry of persisted items. A lot that persists something new picks a tier by these rules and adds its row. The split for settings becomes an attribute of `Setting<Value>` (LOT-060): `scope: .synced | .device`.
+
+### 2. One master per item
+
+An item has exactly one authoritative store and at most one local copy:
+
+- MPStorage items: the forum document is the master; the device keeps the last document read (`base` for LOT-062's merge) and the pending edits. Reads come from the local copy; writes are local-first and synced when a session is available (legacy's sync-first add, which aborted the local change on a network error, is dropped: audit E §7 item 6). On a successful remote read the local list is **merged**, not replaced (legacy `MPStorage.m:202-215` replaced it; audit Q-4).
+- iCloud KVS items: KVS is the master; `UserDefaults` is the mirror that `@AppStorage` and the synchronous `SettingsStore` read. A write goes to both; an external-change notification updates the mirror. The engine never reads KVS on the hot path.
+- A device-only item has no copy.
+
+### 3. Conflict policy
+
+| Store | Policy | Why |
+|---|---|---|
+| MPStorage | per-item three-way merge of LOT-062 (`base`, `ours`, `theirs`), ours wins when both changed, tombstones off until other writers are known to keep them | already decided (LOT-062, Q-6) |
+| iCloud KVS, scalar preferences | **last writer wins per key**, as the store does; on the initial sync (`NSUbiquitousKeyValueStoreInitialSyncChange`) the cloud value wins over the local one | the only conflict is the same setting changed on two devices while offline; the later tap is the user's intent |
+| iCloud KVS, lists (allowlist, super-favourites, smiley favourites) | **last writer wins on the whole list**, each list one key holding `{version, items:[{id, addedAt}]}`; a union merge with tombstones is the documented upgrade if users report lost adds | simplification: these lists change a few times a month; a merge layer would duplicate LOT-062 for three tiny lists |
+| iCloud KVS, reading positions | last writer wins per topic key; the newest `updatedAt` is kept when both devices wrote | a position is a point in time |
+| iCloud account change (`NSUbiquitousKeyValueStoreAccountChange`, sign-out) | the system replaces the store's content with the new Apple ID's data: the app **quarantines** the previous mirror values and any pending KVS write (moved to a device-only file, never uploaded under the new Apple ID), blocks synced reads and writes until the new account's initial sync has completed, then applies the new account's values to the mirror. Device-scoped settings are untouched. The quarantined values are restored only if that Apple ID becomes active again, and deleted after 90 days. A schema version key lets an older build ignore values it cannot read | one Apple ID's data never reaches another Apple ID's store; nothing is lost because the Apple ID changed |
+
+### 4. Offline behaviour
+
+- MPStorage: read from the local copy; edits are queued in the local document and merged on the next successful sync; the UI shows the last sync from `mpstorage_last_rw` (persisted for real, LOT-060). A failed sync never undoes a local edit.
+- iCloud KVS: writes land in the local mirror and in the store's on-device queue; the system uploads later. The app calls `synchronize()` at launch and on foreground, and treats a missing iCloud account as "device-only" without a warning.
+- Device tiers: unaffected.
+
+### 5. Migration from the legacy app (LOT-067 and LOT-158; same bundle id, Q-1)
+
+SwiftHFR ships as an in-place update of `hfrplus.red.super` under the ezzz team, so the legacy container is readable and the legacy data is **kept** (operator 2026-10-28):
+
+1. Import everything into the **device** tiers first, with the LOT-067 plan: UserDefaults keys under their legacy names, `blackListDico.plist` / `whiteList.plist` into the LOT-061 document, `smiley_favorites_cache2` into LOT-064, `composerDraftText` into `DraftContext.legacyGlobal`, Keychain accounts into LOT-065 (device-only item).
+2. Then enable the KVS mirror: for each synced key, if the cloud has no value, push the imported one; if it has one (another device migrated first), the cloud wins (initial-sync rule). Lists follow the same rule, whole list.
+3. MPStorage needs no migration: same thread, same schema `0.1`; the document is re-read on first sync and becomes the merge base.
+4. The legacy keys dropped by LOT-060 are read once where a migration exists (`size_text_topics`), otherwise ignored; nothing is deleted from the legacy container (LOT-067 rule).
+
+### 6. Accounts: device-only by default, opt-in iCloud Keychain sync, optional app lock (Q12)
+
+Accounts stay in a device-only Keychain item (LOT-065, Q-9). Two options, both off by default, are added by LOT-173 ([#312](https://github.com/ezzz/HFRnow/issues/312)):
+
+- **"Synchroniser mes comptes via le trousseau iCloud"**: when on, the credential envelope is also written to a second, **synchronizable** Keychain item (`kSecAttrSynchronizable`, `AfterFirstUnlock`), which iCloud Keychain carries to the user's other devices end to end encrypted. The setting explains what travels and how to stop. Rules of the copy (one item, one envelope, `updatedAt` in the envelope):
+  - *Master.* The device-only item stays the master on each device; every change to it (login, re-login, deletion, main account) is pushed to the synchronizable item while the switch is on.
+  - *Bootstrap.* A device with no device-only item that finds the synchronizable item imports it into a new device-only item and turns the switch on; the imported accounts are not logged in again (the cookies are the session).
+  - *Divergence.* On launch and on foreground, when both items exist and differ, the **newer `updatedAt` wins the whole envelope** (last writer wins, like the KVS lists): a credential refreshed on another device replaces the local copy, a device that was offline longer loses its stale copy. `AccountBook.init(accounts:)` repairs duplicates and the main flag after a replacement; accounts are never silently merged into more than the user had on the winning side.
+  - *Switching off.* Replaces the synchronizable item's envelope with a dated **tombstone** (`{"version":1,"deletedAt":<date>,"accounts":[]}`, no credential) instead of deleting the item, so the other devices receive a positive signal: a device whose switch is on and that reads a tombstone newer than its last push turns its switch off and keeps its device-only item; turning the switch on again anywhere overwrites the tombstone with a full envelope. The **absence** of the item (`errSecItemNotFound`) proves nothing: iCloud Keychain may not have delivered it yet, or the user may have cleared it. It leaves the switch and the device-only item as they are, is retried at the next launch and foreground, and is never a reason to push the local envelope (a push happens only after a credential change on this device or a read of a full envelope). Switching off never deletes a device-only item anywhere.

Supported by static analysis
Script executed: ```bash sed -n '66,82p' docs/adr/0013-storage-tiers.md grep -n 'LOT-173' docs/LOTS.md grep -n -i 'tombstone\|deletedAt\|updatedAt' docs/adr/0013-storage-tiers.md docs/LOTS.md ``` Repository: ezzz/HFRnow Length of output: 7135 ---
**Define how a credential-change push orders against an unread tombstone.** Section 6 orders a tombstone only on the reading side. A device whose switch is on turns it off when the tombstone's `deletedAt` is newer than that device's last push. The ADR does not define the write side. A device that has not read the tombstone can push a full envelope after a credential change. That push overwrites the tombstone, and the ADR does not say whether it should. The device that already switched off keeps its switch off and does not re-read the synchronizable item, so nothing restores the opt-out. Section 6 also describes no queue for the synchronizable item. A proposed "tombstones processed before pending full envelopes" rule would therefore describe a mechanism the ADR does not define. Add the write-side rule to §6 instead. For example, the pushing device could read the synchronizable item and compare `updatedAt` with `deletedAt` before it pushes. `docs/LOTS.md` cites ADR 0013 §6 for LOT-173, so the same §6 rule covers that lot.

+| Tier | Follows | Used for |
+|---|---|---|

+| **Device, not backed up** (`Library/Caches/`, Keychain `ThisDeviceOnly`) | one device | caches, offline pages, **accounts and cookies** (plus an opt-in synchronizable copy, §6) |

+The rules, in order:

+1. **Transferability.** If another platform reads or writes the item today under a known schema, it goes to MPStorage, wire-compatible, and nowhere else as a master. +
+An item has exactly one authoritative store and at most one local copy:
+
+- MPStorage items: the forum document is the master; the device keeps the last document read (`base` for LOT-062's merge) and the pending edits. Reads come from the local copy; writes are local-first and synced when a session is available (legacy's sync-first add, which aborted the local change on a network error, is dropped: audit E §7 item 6). +

+
+- **"Synchroniser mes comptes via le trousseau iCloud"**: when on, the credential envelope is also written to a second, **synchronizable** Keychain item (`kSecAttrSynchronizable`, `AfterFirstUnlock`), which iCloud Keychain carries to the user's other devices end to end encrypted; the device-only item stays the local master; switching off deletes the synchronizable copy. ** Major** · **Data Integrity & Integration** · **Heavy lift** **Make tombstone dominance monotonic across devices.** The existing rule makes a tombstone newer than the last pushed envelope authoritative. The new rule compares `deletedAt` with the local envelope's `updatedAt`, even when that local envelope was not pushed because the item was absent. In `docs/adr/0013-storage-tiers.md`, Line 78 assumes the restored tombstone is newer than the racing device’s `lastPushed`. This sequence contradicts that assumption: 1. Device B reads a full envelope with `enabledAt=50`. 2. Device A writes a tombstone with `deletedAt=150`. 3. Device B completes its stale push and records `lastPushed=200`. 4. +| iCloud KVS, reading positions | last writer wins per topic key; the newest `updatedAt` is kept when both devices wrote | a position is a point in time |
+| iCloud account change (`NSUbiquitousKeyValueStoreAccountChange`, sign-out) | the system replaces the store's content with the new Apple ID's data: the app **quarantines** the previous mirror values and any pending KVS write (moved to a device-only file, never uploaded under the new Apple ID), blocks synced reads and writes until the new account's initial sync has completed, then applies the new account's values to the mirror. Device-scoped settings are untouched. The quarantined values are restored only if that Apple ID becomes active again, and deleted after 90 days. A schema version key lets an older build ignore values it cannot read | one Apple ID's data never reaches another Apple ID's store; nothing is lost because the Apple ID changed |
+
+### 4. Offline behaviour
+
+- MPStorage: read from the local copy; edits are queued in the local document and merged on the next successful sync; the UI shows the last sync from `mpstorage_last_rw` (persisted for real, LOT-060). A failed sync never undoes a local edit.
+- iCloud KVS: writes land in the local mirror and in the store's on-device queue; the system uploads later. The app calls `synchronize()` at launch and on foreground, and treats a missing iCloud account as "device-only" without a warning.
+- Device tiers: unaffected.
+
+### 5. Migration from the legacy app (LOT-067 and LOT-158; same bundle id, Q-1)
+
+SwiftHFR ships as an in-place update of `hfrplus.red.super` under the ezzz team, so the legacy container is readable and the legacy data is **kept** (operator 2026-10-28):
+
+1. Import everything into the **device** tiers first, with the LOT-067 plan: UserDefaults keys under their legacy names, `blackListDico.plist` / `whiteList.plist` into the LOT-061 document, `smiley_favorites_cache2` into LOT-064, `composerDraftText` into `DraftContext.legacyGlobal`, Keychain accounts into LOT-065 (device-only item).
+2. Then enable the KVS mirror: for each synced key, if the cloud has no value, push the imported one; if it has one (another device migrated first), the cloud wins (initial-sync rule). Lists follow the same rule, whole list.
+3. MPStorage needs no migration: same thread, same schema `0.1`; the document is re-read on first sync and becomes the merge base.
+4. The legacy keys dropped by LOT-060 are read once where a migration exists (`size_text_topics`), otherwise ignored; nothing is deleted from the legacy container (LOT-067 rule).
+
+### 6. Accounts: device-only by default, opt-in iCloud Keychain sync, optional app lock (Q12)
+
+Accounts stay in a device-only Keychain item (LOT-065, Q-9). Two options, both off by default, are added by LOT-173 ([#312](https://github.com/ezzz/HFRnow/issues/312)):
+
+- **"Synchroniser mes comptes via le trousseau iCloud"**: when on, the credential envelope is also written to a second, **synchronizable** Keychain item (`kSecAttrSynchronizable`, `AfterFirstUnlock`), which iCloud Keychain carries to the user's other devices end to end encrypted. The setting explains what travels and how to stop. Rules of the copy (one item, one envelope, `updatedAt` in the envelope):
+  - *Master.* The device-only item stays the master on each device; every change to it (login, re-login, deletion, main account) is pushed to the synchronizable item while the switch is on.
+  - *Bootstrap.* A device with no device-only item that finds the synchronizable item imports it into a new device-only item and turns the switch on; the imported accounts are not logged in again (the cookies are the session).
+  - *Divergence.* On launch and on foreground, when both items exist and differ, the **newer `updatedAt` wins the whole envelope** (last writer wins, like the KVS lists): a credential refreshed on another device replaces the local copy, a device that was offline longer loses its stale copy. `AccountBook.init(accounts:)` repairs duplicates and the main flag after a replacement; accounts are never silently merged into more than the user had on the winning side.
+  - *Switching off.* Replaces the synchronizable item's envelope with a dated **tombstone** (`{"version":1,"deletedAt":<date>,"accounts":[]}`, no credential) instead of deleting the item, so the other devices receive a positive signal: a device whose switch is on and that reads a tombstone newer than its last push turns its switch off and keeps its device-only item; turning the switch on again anywhere overwrites the tombstone with a full envelope. The **absence** of the item (`errSecItemNotFound`) proves nothing: iCloud Keychain may not have delivered it yet, or the user may have cleared it. It leaves the switch and the device-only item as they are, is retried at the next launch and foreground, and is never a reason to push the local envelope. Switching off never deletes a device-only item anywhere.
+  - *Write side (every push).* A push is a read-compare-write on the synchronizable item, never a blind write. The envelope carries `enabledAt`, the date of the last explicit switch-on, and each device remembers `lastPushed` (its last write) and `honouredDeletedAt` (the newest tombstone it acted on). Before writing, the device reads the item: a **tombstone** with `deletedAt` newer than `lastPushed` wins, so the device does not push, turns its own switch off, records `honouredDeletedAt` and keeps its device-only item (the local `updatedAt` plays no part: an opt-out is never undone by a credential change, whatever its date); a full envelope newer than the local one is applied first (*Divergence*), then the local change is pushed on top with the same `enabledAt`; an **absent** item is not re-created by a credential change (the push is skipped and retried later). **Only the explicit switch-on action overwrites a tombstone**, writing a full envelope whose `enabledAt` is newer than that `deletedAt`.
+  - *Race repair.* iCloud Keychain has no conditional write, so a device that read a full envelope just before another device wrote the tombstone can still overwrite it. Its envelope betrays the race: `enabledAt` older than the tombstone's `deletedAt`. A device that honoured the tombstone keeps reading the item at launch and foreground while its switch is off; when it finds a full envelope with `enabledAt < honouredDeletedAt`, it re-writes the tombstone (same `deletedAt`). The racing device's next read-compare then sees a tombstone newer than its `lastPushed` and switches off. Tombstone dominance is therefore monotonic: a tombstone yields only to a later explicit switch-on, never to a push.
